title: Plugins and engine extensions
summary: Connect optional engine features to renderer initialization, pass registration and disposal.

blocks.text: IPlugin requires a unique name and can implement install, registerPasses, dispose and priority. Scene.use installs/replaces by name; removePlugin disposes and unregisters render features. SceneComposer also owns feature registration. Lower numeric priority executes earlier for render pass insertion.

OutlinePlugin is a public retiam export. Its registerPasses constructs OutlinePass using io.resolvedColor, adds it to the graph and replaces io.resolvedColor with presentationOutput, connecting the result to subsequent passes. Follow the [custom plugin tutorial](/tutorial-custom-plugin) to build both a behavior plugin and a rendering feature.

A plugin can also install scene settings or tasks without adding GPU passes. Read composer availability in install: a detached Scene can install a plugin before a GPU context exists, so initialization must account for attachment timing.

items: Own and dispose task handles, DOM listeners, buffers and textures created by the plugin.
Preserve the render-graph input/output chain and declare every resource dependency.
Choose stable names for replacement/removal and avoid retaining a disposed instance.
Document whether configuration changes rebuild shader code, graph structure or only a uniform.

blocks.text: One plugin owns one updater and stops that exact task during disposal.
